To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
the beamforming system is a viable solution for electronically scanned RF-to-bites beam aperture arrays.

(a) a beamforming system based 2-D spatially bandpass IIR plane wave filtering can provide significant gain in the BER performance of the RF receiver chain; (b) a beamforming receiver chain based on 2-D spatial filtering is a viable option for electronically scanned RF-to-bit beam aperture arrays.

(i) 2-D spatially bandpass IIR filters can be used to electronically scan the beam aperture of a RF-to-bits array and (ii) the proposed beamforming system can be implemented in real-time in CMOS technology.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the design and development of RF-to-bits electronically scanned beam aperture arrays for high resolution imaging and radar applications.
design and implementation aspects for an electronically scanned beam aperture array using 2-D spatially bandpass filters.
the development of an RF beamforming system that can be integrated with a 3D antenna array to realize an electronically scanned RF-to-bites beam aperture array.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the 2-D I.I.R. spatially bandpass filtering approach is feasible for beamforming in wideband electronically scanned arrays.
a 2-D spatially bandpass beamforming system is feasible for a wideband electronically scanned beam antenna array.
2-D IRR beamforming systems can be implemented using 5-bit ADCs and 8-bit arithmetic precision with a real time operating speed of 429 MS/s.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
a beamforming system based 2-D IIF plane wave filtering can potentially achieve real-time beamforming with a 2-bit quantization of RF signals and 5-bit ADC precision.
the proposed beamforming system provides an effective way to realize electronically scanned RF-to-bit aperture arrays with high gain and low BER performance.

we have proposed a new class of 2-D spatially bandpass filters for beamforming in RF-to-bits systems and presented a design methodology that is based on the multi-dimensional spatio-tempo spectral analysis and 1st-order analysis of the beamforming filter.
The main takeaway from our work is that
a wideband beamforming system using a 2-D IRR spatially bandpass filters is a promising approach for future RF to bits beam aperture arrays.
a 2-D IIF beamformer with a fixed beam angle can be realized using a 2-D $$z$$z-domain plane wave filter.
a 2-D IIF beam filter can be implemented in a single chip and can be used for beamforming applications in electronically scanned arrays.
